text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.
LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index leapt to a record closing high on Thursday as Wall Street rose close to all-time peaks and gilts surged after a drop in UK inflation.
With the market also boosted by a decision to leave UK interest rates unchanged, the FTSE 100 index closed 38.6 points higher at 4,197.5, its second record close of the year so far.

FRANKFURT - German shares turned higher after a slow start on Thursday, with the DAX led up by the futures market to fresh record highs and coming tantalisingly close to the magical 3,000-point level.

The DAX closed the bourse session up 4.86 points at a record closing high of 2,993.31, having earlier hit a record intra-day high of 2,998.61 and having risen over 20 points from an early low of 2,970.45. In post-bourse trade the index was rose 19.56 to 2,996.12.
PARIS - French stocks closed at a record high on Thursday and the market remained in a bullish mood despite the Bank of France's inaction on interest rates.
The market was supported by gains on Wall Street, a strong dollar and rising debt markets in France.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 19.79 points or 0.83 percent at 2,407.77. The CAC-40 futures contract was down two points at 2,408.
ZURICH - The Swiss bourse closed firmer on broad front with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closing over 4,000 points for the first time.
The rise was due to technical factors, favourable bond markets, firming European bourses and strong advances in Roche certificates and major banks.
The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) soared 17.10 points, or 0.67 percent, to 2,568.85 points.
The SMI was up 0.69 percent, or 27.5 points, to 4,007.1.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended a little higher after swinging between positive and negative zones.
Shares in some blue-chip firms continued to firm, but overall gains were limited by the financial sector, which has been dragged down since the end of last year.
The Nikkei 225 average finished up 51.21 points or 0.28 percent at 18,144.34.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index scored another all-time closing high on Thursday, as investors snatched up stocks which were left behind in Wednesday's record-breaking rally.

The Hang Seng index soared above the 14,000 point-level for the first time this session, hitting a record high of 14,004.93 before closing on a gain of 64.03 points at 13,830.68. Turnover was a massive HK$16.23 billion, the third largest ever.
SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended the way it started on Thursday, just weaker and narrowly mixed, with a firmer resources sector failing to overcome a Dow-weakened industrials group.

The market spent most of its day meandering in a five point range with only a late burst of interest in bellwether BHP and National Australia Bank bringing the benchmark indicator back to within a whisker of square.
The All Ordinaries index lost just 1.9 points to 2,436.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares had a healthy Thursday and ended firmly in positive territory after being helped by a firmer gold sector and a bullish short-term outlook for major international markets, dealers said.
The all-share index rose 27.6 points to finish at 6,779 as the industrials index jumped 45.7 points to 8,176.4.

Gold shares had a good day with the index rising just under percent, or 12.6 points, to 1,421 as the first day of the quarterly reporting season kicked off with Goldfields announcing healthy third quarter results.
